Appoint and maintain a U.S.-citizen Security Officer eligible for a Secret-level or higher clearance.
Provide Cable System Information to the Compliance Monitoring Agencies within the specified deadlines.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S.-bound and U.S.-originating traffic on the cable system.
Provide lists of Covered Third Parties, Principal Equipment, and Service Providers as required.
Obtain prior written non-objection before deploying certain flagged Principal Equipment.

entries.label: Telecom Services Network Ltd
entries.text:
Designate a U.S. Law Enforcement Point of Contact, subject to DOJ approval, and make U.S. Records available within five business days of lawful process.
Do not disclose U.S. Records or Domestic Communications to a non-U.S. government without satisfying U.S. law and obtaining DOJ consent or U.S. court authorization.
Provide DOJ annual tax records, filed returns, financial statements, and related reconciliation.
Notify DOJ at least 60 days before beginning interconnected VoIP services or becoming a facilities-based provider, and comply with CALEA and lawful interception requirements.

entries.label: BRUSA Cable System
entries.text:
Provide BRUSA Cable System information, including network maps, operational details, maintenance and security contracts, and restoration plans.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt traffic to and from the United States and enable the network operations center to suspend or interrupt the cable system.
Provide and update lists of principal equipment and its vendors, contractors, and subcontractors.
Give advance notice of material equipment modifications and changes to principal-equipment vendors or support.
Report unauthorized access, disruptions, disclosures, or material breaches and cooperate with remediation.
Submit annual compliance reports and allow USG Parties reasonable-notice visits to inspect the domestic communications infrastructure.

entries.label: BRUSA Cable System
entries.text:
Provide BRUSA Cable System information, including network maps, contracts, and restoration plans.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S. traffic on the cable system.
Report unauthorized access, disruptions, disclosures, or material breaches within 10 business days of discovery.
Give advance notice of material equipment modifications and changes to vendors or subcontractors.
Submit an annual compliance report to the USG Parties.

entries.label: Telekomunikasi Indonesia International (USA) Inc.
entries.text:
Route domestic communications through U.S. points of presence so lawful U.S. surveillance can be conducted.
Locate principal equipment used for domestic communications in the United States, subject to permitted exceptions.
Maintain network operations centers supporting domestic communications or infrastructure within the United States using screened personnel.
Store specified communications, transactional data, call-associated data, billing records, and subscriber information in the United States.

entries.label: Telroaming
entries.text:
Designate and maintain a U.S. law enforcement point of contact subject to DOJ approval.
Designate and maintain a U.S. citizen security officer in the United States, unless DOJ agrees otherwise in writing.
Screen personnel who have access to U.S. communications, equipment, lawful process, or records.
Report known or suspected security incidents to DOJ within 72 hours.
Keep information responsive to lawful U.S. process within the United States, unless an exception applies.

entries.label: SAm-1 Cable System
entries.text:
Maintain a U.S.-citizen Security Point of Contact available 24/7 for CMA concerns.
Provide SAm-1 system information and updated peering and interconnection lists to the CMAs.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S. traffic on SAm-1.
Report specified security incidents, breaches, and material LOA violations to the CMAs within 48 hours.

entries.label: BRUSA Cable System
entries.text:
Maintain a U.S.-citizen Security Point of Contact available 24/7 for national security or law-enforcement concerns.
Provide BRUSA system information, including network maps, equipment, vendors, and restoration plans, upon required deadlines or CMA request.
Maintain the ability to interrupt U.S.-bound or U.S.-originating traffic and suspend BRUSA communications functionality.
Report specified security incidents, unauthorized access, disclosures, and material breaches to the CMAs within 48 hours.
Obtain DoD approval before deploying distributed acoustic sensing technology on the marine portion of the cable.

entries.label: Telxius Cable Puerto Rico, Inc.
entries.text:
Designate and maintain a U.S. law-enforcement point of contact approved by DOJ and the FBI.
Screen personnel who have access to U.S. records, domestic communications, or domestic communications infrastructure.
Provide U.S. records promptly in response to lawful U.S. process, generally within five days.
Do not disclose U.S. records, domestic communications infrastructure, or domestic communications to foreign governments, entities, or persons without DOJ approval or a U.S. court order.
Report security incidents and specified breaches to DOJ within 48 hours.

entries.label: Telxius Cable Puerto Rico, Inc.
entries.text:
Maintain a U.S.-citizen Security Point of Contact available 24/7 for national security and law-enforcement concerns.
Provide PCCS system information, equipment lists, and vendor information to the Compliance Monitoring Agencies on the specified schedules.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S.-bound and U.S.-originating PCCS traffic and configure the NOC to suspend or interrupt PCCS communications.
Implement logical and physical security measures, personnel screening, incident reporting, and related security policies.
Submit annual compliance reports and permit CMA audits and facility visits.

entries.label: MAREA Cable System
entries.text:
Maintain a U.S.-citizen security point of contact available around the clock for national-security or law-enforcement concerns.
Provide cable-system information, equipment lists, and vendor information to the compliance-monitoring agencies on the required schedule.
Maintain the ability to interrupt traffic to and from the United States and configure the network operations center to suspend MAREA communications.
Report qualifying security incidents, unauthorized access, and material breaches to the agencies within 48 hours.

entries.label: SAm-1 Cable System
entries.text:
Designate U.S.-citizen security points of contact who reside in the United States and are available 24/7.
Provide cable system information, including network details, maintenance and security contracts, and restoration plans.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S. traffic and enable the network operations center to suspend or interrupt the cable system.
Take reasonable cybersecurity, physical security, personnel-screening, and incident-reporting measures.

entries.label: Tikal-AMX3
entries.text:
Appoint and maintain Security Officers responsible for overseeing compliance with the agreement.
Provide cable system information, including network maps and restoration plans, to the CMAs.
Maintain the ability to interrupt U.S.-bound traffic and configure the NOC to suspend or interrupt communications.
Report Covered Third Parties, Principal Equipment, and Service Providers to the CMAs and obtain required non-objections.

entries.label: SAm-1 Cable System
entries.text:
Maintain a U.S.-citizen security point of contact residing in the United States.
Provide DHS with cable system information, equipment lists, and vendor information on the stated timelines.
Maintain the ability to interrupt U.S. traffic and suspend or interrupt the SAm-1 optical signal.
Take practicable measures to prevent unauthorized logical access and physically secure the domestic communications infrastructure.
Report qualifying security incidents, unauthorized access, disclosures, or material breaches to DHS.

entries.label: Trans Americas Fiber Cable (TAM-1)
entries.text:
Appoint and maintain a U.S.-citizen Security Officer eligible for a Secret-level or higher clearance to oversee LOA compliance.
Provide Cable System Information, including network maps, maintenance contracts, IRU or lease holders, and restoration plans.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S.-bound or U.S.-originating traffic and configure the NOC to suspend or interrupt TAM-1 communications.
Provide lists of Covered Third Parties, Principal Equipment, and relevant service providers, with advance notice for specified additions or changes.
Take practicable measures to prevent unauthorized logical access and unlawful use or disclosure of information carried on TAM-1.

entries.label: TvF Cloud, Inc.
entries.text:
Comply with applicable lawful interception laws, including CALEA, and lawful U.S. process.
Submit a DOJ-reviewed Network and Systems Security Plan within 75 days.
Store all U.S. Records at specified data centers in Virginia and California.
Nominate a DOJ-approved U.S.-based law enforcement point of contact.
Provide annual compliance reports to DOJ beginning December 1, 2018.

entries.label: US Matrix Telecommunications, Inc.
entries.text:
Make U.S. customer billing, subscriber, and related records available in the United States in response to lawful U.S. process.
Provide DOJ with updated security architecture and domestic communications infrastructure diagrams within 30 days after FCC consent.
Notify DOJ of unauthorized disclosures of U.S. Records within five business days of learning of them.
Maintain a U.S. point of presence and point of contact to receive service of process and support lawful surveillance requests.
Notify DOJ of cyber threats or cyber incidents affecting systems used for U.S. domestic communications services within five business days.

entries.label: USConnect Holdings, LLC
entries.text:
The agencies have no objection to removing the condition on USConnect’s international 214 authorization.
The removed condition required compliance with national security, law enforcement, and public safety commitments in the May 18, 2005 Letter of Assurance.

entries.label: California-Hawaii S1 Cable System (CHI)
entries.text:
Appoint and maintain a security officer for each Licensee.
Provide cable system information, including network maps and restoration plans, to the CMAs.
Maintain the ability to promptly interrupt U.S. traffic on CHI.
Provide lists and advance notice concerning covered third parties, principal equipment, and third-party service providers.

entries.label: Vocus Group Limited
entries.text:
Vocus agrees to permit disclosure of confidential FCC submissions to specified federal departments, agencies, and offices.
Vocus acknowledges that the Committee may terminate the LOA if mitigation is no longer warranted.
Vocus acknowledges that termination does not eliminate liability for breaches occurring while the LOA was in effect.
Vocus acknowledges that the FCC will be notified of no objection to granting the application after execution of the LOA.

entries.label: World Mobile Networks
entries.text:
Submit updated cybersecurity and system security plans to DOJ within 60 days of FCC approval and annually thereafter.
Provide DOJ lists of countries from which covered equipment, records, lawful process, communications, or infrastructure are accessed.
Report known or suspected security incidents to DOJ within 48 hours.
Provide DOJ a principal equipment list within 30 days of FCC approval and annually thereafter.

entries.label: Zayo Group, LLC
entries.text:
Comply with the commitments and undertakings in the January 21, 2020 Letter of Agreement.
Provide the additional commitments set forth in the Letter of Agreement.
Allow the Commission to condition approval on compliance with the Letter of Agreement.

entries.label: CBTS Technology Solutions LLC
entries.text:
The Committee requests removal of the license condition requiring compliance with the October 10, 2024 mitigation agreement.
The Committee terminated the mitigation agreement because it determined the mitigation is no longer warranted.
The Commission is asked to notify the Committee when the license condition has been changed.
